nodes.name: When Executed by Another Workflow
nodes.notes: Expects: project_key, ticket_id, title, description, translated_title, translated_description, requester_email. Optional: comment_id - which comment attachments are read from. Omit for first contact; follow-up callers pass the latest customer comment id.

nodes.name: TEST trigger
nodes.notes: TEST HARNESS ONLY. Lets this sub-workflow be run standalone against a real ticket.

values.content:
You are an information extraction system for customer support messages.

Extract every email address that the customer has provided as their own account or contact address.

Return only a JSON object that matches the provided schema.

Rules:
- The output must contain exactly one key: customer_emails, an array of strings.
- If the message contains no qualifying email address, return an empty array.
- Include every distinct qualifying address, in the order in which they appear.
- Copy each address exactly as written. Do not guess, infer, reconstruct, correct, complete or fabricate an address.
- Do not include duplicates.
- Return at most 5 addresses. If more are present, return the first 5.
- If the message contains forwarded content (often labelled with "Forwarded message") disregard everything that comes after that and only consider the content before it in the analysis.
- Also disregard quoted replies from our own support team: everything from a line such as "On <date> ... wrote:", "From: ...", "-----Original Message-----", or any line beginning with ">".
- Exclude our own addresses: support@, no-reply@, noreply@, do-not-reply@, any address on our own company or helpdesk domain, and any address belonging to one of our support agents.
- Exclude addresses that plainly belong to someone other than the customer, for example a bank, a payment provider, a legal representative or an unrelated third party mentioned in passing.
- Do not include markdown, explanations, comments or extra text.

nodes.name: Any images to read?
nodes.notes: Requires images AND ocr_model_id. Without a model it degrades to body-only extraction.

nodes.name: Loop over emails
nodes.notes: A 200 exits without looping back, so the first hit wins and the rest are never queried.

nodes.name: Edit Fields (search)
nodes.notes: HMAC is rebuilt per iteration - nonce-based replay protection means a signature cannot be reused.

nodes.name: Response code switch
nodes.notes: 404 and Fallback both loop back for the next address, so a payments outage looks like a miss rather than raising.

parameters.content:
# BrainIQ prod - Email extraction and lookup

Brand copy of `CS - Email extraction and lookup [Template]`.

Called from BOTH BrainIQ flows when the requester own address is NOT found in the payments database:
- `BrainIQ prod - Main automation flow` (first contact, omits comment_id)
- `BrainIQ prod - 2nd message trigger` (follow-up, passes the latest customer comment id)

**Input:** project_key, ticket_id, title, description, translated_title, translated_description, requester_email, optional comment_id

**Returns one item with an `outcome`:**
- `matched` - plus the bot/search response spread at top level, plus matched_email and matched_email_source
- `all_emails_failed`
- `no_email_found`

## Brand-specific
Zendesk + OpenAI credentials are BrainIQ. `Call CS - HMAC` points at `BrainIQ prod - HMAC`.

## Config needed
`ocr_model_id` must be set to a vision-capable model or image reading is skipped and only the body is scanned.
